title: Overnight Oats with Berries
description: Make four jars on Sunday night and breakfast is decided until Wednesday. No cooking whatsoever.
steps: Divide the oats and chia seeds between four jars.
Pour in the milk and add the yoghurt and honey. Stir each one properly — dry pockets stay dry overnight.
Top with the berries, seal, and refrigerate at least 6 hours.
Eat cold, loosening with a splash of milk if it has set too firm.

title: Peanut Butter and Banana Overnight Oats
description: The higher-protein version. Add the banana in the morning or it browns in the jar.
steps: Warm the peanut butter slightly so it stirs in rather than clumping.
Mix the oats, milk, yoghurt, peanut butter, honey and cinnamon and divide between four jars.
Refrigerate at least 6 hours.
Slice the banana over the top the morning you eat it.

title: Egg and Vegetable Muffins
description: Twelve baked egg cups from one tray. Grab two on the way out, hot or cold, for three days.
steps: Heat the oven to 180°C and oil a 12-hole muffin tin thoroughly.
Soften the onion and capsicum in the oil for 6 minutes, then wilt the spinach through. Cool slightly.
Beat the eggs with the milk, paprika and plenty of salt, then stir in the vegetables and cheese.
Fill each hole three quarters full and bake 22 minutes until puffed and just set.
Cool 5 minutes before lifting them out, or they tear.

title: Greek Yoghurt with Honey and Walnuts
description: Three ingredients, three minutes, and more protein than most cooked breakfasts.
steps: Spoon the yoghurt into a bowl.
Pour the honey over and scatter the walnuts and cinnamon.

title: Scrambled Eggs on Toast
description: Low heat and constant movement is the whole technique. Reheated scrambled egg is rubber, so make what you will eat.
steps: Beat the eggs with the milk and a good pinch of salt.
Melt the butter in a cold pan over low heat, then pour the eggs in.
Stir constantly with a spatula, pulling the set curds in from the edges, for about 5 minutes.
Take the pan off the heat while the eggs still look slightly underdone — they carry on cooking.
Pile onto toast and grind pepper over.

title: Banana Oat Pancakes
description: Blended in one go, no separate flour. Stack the spares between paper and they keep two days.
steps: Blend the oats to a rough flour, then add the bananas, eggs, milk, baking powder and cinnamon and blend smooth.
Rest the batter 5 minutes — it thickens noticeably.
Cook in butter over medium heat, a ladle at a time, until bubbles hold on the surface, then flip.
Serve with honey and berries.

title: Breakfast Shakshuka for One
description: Built from a jar of sauce you already made. Two eggs poached in ten minutes.
steps: Fry the garlic and spices in the oil for 30 seconds.
Add the tomatoes and simmer 4 minutes until thickened.
Make two wells, crack the eggs in, cover, and cook 5 minutes.
Scatter the feta over and serve with the toast.

title: Bacon and Egg Roll
description: The weekend one. Ten minutes and it has to be eaten straight away.
steps: Fry the bacon until the edges crisp, then set aside in the pan's warm corner.
Fry the eggs in the bacon fat, basting the whites, until the yolk is still soft.
Butter the split rolls and toast them cut-side down in the same pan.
Build with bacon, egg and tomato sauce.

title: Berry Protein Smoothie
description: Two minutes in a blender. Drink it immediately — it separates within the hour.
steps: Put everything in a blender with the liquid at the bottom.
Blend 60 seconds until completely smooth.
Loosen with more milk if it is too thick to drink.

title: Avocado and Feta Toast
description: Five minutes. Avocado goes brown quickly, so there is no making this ahead.
steps: Toast the bread.
Mash the avocado roughly with the lemon juice and salt — leave some texture.
Spread thickly, then crumble the feta over.
Finish with the oil and chilli flakes.

title: Porridge with Honey and Banana
description: The cheapest breakfast there is. Eight minutes on the stove, or three in a microwave.
steps: Simmer the oats with the milk and a pinch of salt for 6 minutes, stirring, until thick.
Take off the heat and rest 2 minutes — it thickens further.
Top with the banana, honey, cinnamon and walnuts.

title: Breakfast Burrito
description: Roll four, wrap them in foil, and reheat one each morning. The one make-ahead hot breakfast that genuinely works.
steps: Fry the bacon until crisp, then set aside.
Warm the beans with the paprika and mash roughly.
Scramble the eggs in the oil over low heat, stopping while still soft.
Lay beans, egg, bacon, cheese and spring onion down the middle of each tortilla, fold the ends in and roll tightly.
Toast seam-side down in a dry pan for 2 minutes.
To store: wrap each in foil and reheat 90 seconds in a microwave.

title: Chia Pudding
description: Five minutes of stirring, three days of breakfasts. Stir once after ten minutes or the seeds clump at the bottom.
steps: Whisk the chia seeds into the milk with the honey and vanilla.
Leave 10 minutes, then whisk again — this is the step that decides whether it sets evenly.
Divide between four jars and refrigerate at least 4 hours.
Top with berries and almonds before eating.

title: Garlic Mushrooms on Toast
description: Get the pan properly hot and do not crowd it, or the mushrooms stew instead of browning.
steps: Heat the butter and oil until foaming, then add the mushrooms in one layer and leave them alone for 3 minutes.
Toss and cook a further 4 minutes until deep brown.
Add the garlic for the last 30 seconds and season well.
Pile onto toast with the parsley and parmesan.

title: Homemade Baked Beans on Toast
description: Better than the tin and barely more work. Make a batch and reheat a ladle at a time all week.
steps: Soften the onion in the oil for 8 minutes, then add the garlic, paprika and tomato paste.
Add the tomatoes, sugar and vinegar and simmer 10 minutes.
Fold the beans through and cook 8 minutes more, crushing a few against the pan to thicken.
Season hard and spoon over toast.

title: Bircher Muesli
description: Grated apple does the sweetening, so it needs very little honey. Keeps three days and softens as it goes.
steps: Toss the grated apple with the lemon juice straight away so it does not brown.
Mix the oats, milk, yoghurt, honey and cinnamon, then fold the apple through.
Refrigerate overnight.
Loosen with milk and scatter the almonds over before eating.

title: Spinach and Feta Omelette
description: Six minutes, thirty grams of protein. Take it off the heat while the middle still looks wet.
steps: Wilt the spinach in the oil for 1 minute and push it to one side of the pan.
Beat the eggs with salt and pour them in.
Draw the setting edges into the middle and tilt the pan so the raw egg runs out.
Scatter the feta over, fold in half while the centre is still slightly soft, and slide onto a plate.

title: Peanut Butter and Banana Toast
description: Three minutes standing at the bench. Sometimes that is the entire requirement.
steps: Toast the bread and spread with the peanut butter while it is still hot so it melts in.
Lay the banana over and finish with honey and cinnamon.

title: Breakfast Quesadilla
description: Egg and cheese pressed between tortillas. Ten minutes, and it must be eaten crisp.
steps: Scramble the eggs softly in the butter with the paprika.
Spread over two tortillas with the cheese and spring onion, then top with the others.
Toast in a dry pan for 3 minutes a side, pressing down with a spatula, until the cheese has melted and the outside is crisp.
Cut into wedges.

title: Smoked Salmon Bagel
description: No cooking beyond the toaster. High protein and on the table in five minutes.
steps: Split and toast the bagels.
Spread thickly with cream cheese.
Lay the salmon over, then the onion, capers and dill.
Squeeze the lemon over and grind on plenty of pepper.

title: Sweet Potato Hash with Eggs
description: The hash keeps two days; crack fresh eggs over it each morning. A weekend breakfast that stretches into the week.
steps: Fry the bacon in a wide pan until its fat runs, then set aside.
Add the oil and the sweet potato in one layer and leave it alone for 5 minutes so it browns rather than steams.
Toss, add the onion and capsicum, and cook 10 minutes more.
Add the garlic, paprika and bacon and season well.
Make eight wells, crack in the eggs, cover, and cook 6 minutes.
Finish with spring onion.

title: Yoghurt and Granola Parfait
description: Assembled in three minutes. Layer it just before eating so the granola stays crunchy.
steps: Spoon half the yoghurt into a glass, then half the granola and berries.
Repeat, and finish with the honey.

title: Cheese and Tomato Toastie
description: Butter the outside of the bread, not the pan — that is the whole trick to an even crust.
steps: Salt the tomato slices and pat them dry.
Spread mustard on the inside faces, then add cheese and tomato and close.
Butter the outside of both slices.
Toast in a dry pan over medium-low heat for 4 minutes a side, pressing down, until deep gold.

title: Boiled Eggs with Toast Soldiers
description: Six minutes exactly, from boiling water, for a runny yolk and a set white.
steps: Lower the eggs into already-boiling water and set a timer for 6 minutes.
Toast and butter the bread and cut it into strips.
Sit the eggs in cups, take the tops off, and season.

title: Warm Breakfast Couscous
description: Couscous needs only boiling liquid, so this is faster than porridge and keeps two days.
steps: Bring the milk to a simmer with the honey and cinnamon.
Pour it over the couscous and apricots, cover, and leave 5 minutes.
Fork through to separate the grains.
Top with the apple and almonds.
